title: Homeowners forms and Section I coverages
summary: Match HO-2 through HO-8 to who they fit and how they cover, then learn Coverages A to D, the special limits and key additional coverages.
objectives: Match each homeowners form to its perils basis and who it fits
Place a property loss under Coverage A, B, C or D
Apply the 2011 Coverage C special limits, including the theft-only limits
Recall the tree and ordinance or law additional coverages

scenes.title: Homeowners forms and Section I coverages
scenes.subtitle: ISO 2011 homeowners program (05 11 forms); HO-2, HO-5 and HO-8 checked in the 2000 forms

beats.text: Homeowners is 15% of your exam: 22 items. This lesson covers the forms and the property coverages.
beats.say: Homeowners is fifteen percent of your exam: twenty two items. This lesson covers the forms and the property coverages.

beats.text: Dollar amounts come from the 2011 forms unless another edition is named. The newer 2022 forms changed some of them.
beats.say: Dollar amounts come from the twenty eleven forms unless another edition is named. The newer twenty twenty two forms changed some of them.

scenes.title: Broad, Special, Comprehensive
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 02 10 00; HO 00 03 05 11; HO 00 05 10 00, Sec. I Perils Insured Against; AIC 43 (eligibility)

columns.name: HO-2 Broad
points: Named perils on A, B and C
Same 16 perils as HO-3 Coverage C

columns.name: HO-3 Special
points: Open perils on A and B
16 named perils on C, including theft

columns.name: HO-5 Comprehensive
points: Open perils on A, B and C

scenes.tell: Count the open-perils coverages: HO-2 none, HO-3 the buildings only, HO-5 buildings and personal property.

beats.text: Start with three forms for the owner-occupant of a 1- to 4-family dwelling. HO-2, the Broad Form, covers the dwelling, other structures and personal property for named perils only.
beats.say: Start with three forms for the owner-occupant of a one to four family dwelling. H O two, the Broad Form, covers the dwelling, other structures and personal property for named perils only.

beats.text: HO-3, the Special Form, covers the dwelling and other structures for open perils: any direct physical loss not excluded. Personal property gets 16 named perils, including theft.
beats.say: H O three, the Special Form, covers the dwelling and other structures for open perils: any direct physical loss not excluded. Personal property gets sixteen named perils, including theft.

beats.text: HO-5, the Comprehensive Form, is open perils on all three. The quick tell: count the open-perils coverages.
beats.say: H O five, the Comprehensive Form, is open perils on all three. The quick tell: count the open-perils coverages.

scenes.title: A number peg for the forms
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 04 05 11; HO 00 06 05 11; HO 00 08 10 00; AIC 43; adapted from memory hook mn_prop-13
scenes.hook: HO-2 Broad: a named list. HO-3 Special: the house is open. HO-4: renters. HO-5: high-five, open on everything. HO-6: the condo unit. HO-8: older homes.
items: HO-4, tenants: Coverages C and D only, no A or B
HO-6, condo unit owners and co-op shareholders: A covers fixtures and improvements
HO-8 (2000 edition): 10 named perils; theft on premises only, up to $1,000

beats.text: A number peg: HO-2 Broad, a named list. HO-3 Special, the house is open. HO-4, renters. HO-5, high-five, open on everything. HO-6, the condo unit. HO-8, older homes.
beats.say: A number peg: H O two Broad, a named list. H O three Special, the house is open. H O four, renters. H O five, high five, open on everything. H O six, the condo unit. H O eight, older homes.

beats.text: HO-4 is for tenants: Coverages C and D only, no A or B.
beats.say: H O four is for tenants: Coverages C and D only, no A or B.

beats.text: HO-6 is for condo unit owners and co-op shareholders. Its Coverage A isn't the whole building: it covers the unit's alterations, appliances, fixtures and improvements.
beats.say: H O six is for condo unit owners and co-op shareholders. Its Coverage A isn't the whole building: it covers the unit's alterations, appliances, fixtures and improvements.

beats.text: HO-8, in the 2000 edition, fits older homes whose replacement cost far exceeds market value. Theft is covered only on premises, up to $1,000 per loss.
beats.say: H O eight, in the two thousand edition, fits older homes whose replacement cost far exceeds market value. Theft is covered only on premises, up to one thousand dollars per loss.

scenes.q: Which homeowners form insures the dwelling on an open-perils basis but personal property only for named perils?
scenes.why: HO-3 is open perils on Coverages A and B and named perils on Coverage C. HO-2 is named perils on all three; HO-5 is open perils on all three.

beats.text: Quick check. Which form covers the dwelling on open perils, but personal property only for named perils? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. Which form covers the dwelling on open perils, but personal property only for named perils? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: HO-3, the Special Form: the house is open perils, your belongings named perils.
reveal.say: H O three, the Special Form: the house is open perils, your belongings named perils.

scenes.title: Section I: Coverages A to D (2011 HO-3)
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverages A–D
items: 10% of A; does not reduce A
Living expense and fair rental value

beats.text: Coverage A is the dwelling and structures attached to it, like an attached garage. The land is not covered.
beats.say: Coverage A is the dwelling and structures attached to it, like an attached garage. The land is not covered.

beats.text: Coverage B is other structures set apart by clear space, like a detached shed. It's 10% of Coverage A, and using it does not reduce A.
beats.say: Coverage B is other structures set apart by clear space, like a detached shed. It's ten percent of Coverage A, and using it does not reduce A.

beats.text: Coverage C is personal property, anywhere in the world. But property usually kept at another residence, or in self-storage, is limited to 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater.
beats.say: Coverage C is personal property, anywhere in the world. But property usually kept at another residence, or in self-storage, is limited to ten percent of C or one thousand dollars, whichever is greater.

beats.text: Coverage D, Loss of Use, is one limit for additional living expense and fair rental value. If a civil authority prohibits use of the home because of covered damage next door, it pays up to 2 weeks.
beats.say: Coverage D, Loss of Use, is one limit for additional living expense and fair rental value. If a civil authority prohibits use of the home because of covered damage next door, it pays up to two weeks.

scenes.title: Belongings at the cottage
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverage C.1–C.2
scenes.story: Maya has a 2011 HO-3 with a $60,000 Coverage C limit. She keeps belongings with an actual cash value of $9,000 at her own cottage up north, a second residence. A covered fire destroys them. How much is paid, ignoring the deductible?

items.label: Fire is a named peril
items.detail: Coverage C covers her property anywhere in the world

items.label: But it's usually kept at another residence
items.detail: Limit: 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater

beats.text: Maya's Coverage C limit is $60,000. She keeps $9,000 of belongings at her own cottage up north, and a fire destroys them. What does her HO-3 pay?
beats.say: Maya's Coverage C limit is sixty thousand dollars. She keeps nine thousand dollars of belongings at her own cottage up north, and a fire destroys them. What does her H O three pay?

beats.text: Fire is a covered peril, and Coverage C goes anywhere. But property usually kept at another residence is limited to 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater.
beats.say: Fire is a covered peril, and Coverage C goes anywhere. But property usually kept at another residence is limited to ten percent of C or one thousand dollars, whichever is greater.

beats.text: 10% of $60,000 is $6,000. That beats $1,000, so the policy pays $6,000.
beats.say: Ten percent of sixty thousand dollars is six thousand dollars. That beats one thousand dollars, so the policy pays six thousand dollars.

scenes.title: Coverage C special limits (2011 HO-3)
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverage C.3.a–i
items: Theft of firearms; theft of silverware

beats.text: Some property has a special limit per loss. Money and coins: $200. Securities, deeds and passports: $1,500. Watercraft, with trailers and motors: $1,500.
beats.say: Some property has a special limit per loss. Money and coins: two hundred dollars. Securities, deeds and passports: one thousand five hundred dollars. Watercraft, with trailers and motors: one thousand five hundred dollars.

beats.text: Now the trap. Jewelry, watches and furs: $1,500, but only for theft. Firearms and silverware: $2,500 each, also only for theft.
beats.say: Now the trap. Jewelry, watches and furs: one thousand five hundred dollars, but only for theft. Firearms and silverware: two thousand five hundred dollars each, also only for theft.

beats.text: Business property: $2,500 on premises, $1,500 away. These limits don't increase Coverage C.
beats.say: Business property: two thousand five hundred dollars on premises, one thousand five hundred dollars away. These limits don't increase Coverage C.

scenes.q: Under the 2011 HO-3, a fire destroys jewelry with an actual cash value of $4,000. Coverage C is $80,000. Ignoring the deductible, the policy pays:
scenes.why: The $1,500 jewelry special limit applies only to loss by theft. A fire loss is paid in full, within the Coverage C limit.

beats.text: Your turn. A fire destroys jewelry with an actual cash value of $4,000. Coverage C is $80,000. Ignoring the deductible, what does the 2011 HO-3 pay? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. A fire destroys jewelry with an actual cash value of four thousand dollars. Coverage C is eighty thousand dollars. Ignoring the deductible, what does the twenty eleven H O three pay? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: $4,000. The jewelry limit applies only to theft. If a burglar had taken it, the most paid would be $1,500.
reveal.say: Four thousand dollars. The jewelry limit applies only to theft. If a burglar had taken it, the most paid would be one thousand five hundred dollars.

scenes.title: Additional coverages (2011 HO-3)
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Additional Coverages E.1.b, E.3, E.11

items.label: Trees and plants: $500 per tree, not windstorm
Tree removal per loss, $500 per tree

beats.text: Trees, shrubs and plants get up to 5% of Coverage A, $500 per tree. Their perils include theft and vandalism, but not windstorm.
beats.say: Trees, shrubs and plants get up to five percent of Coverage A, five hundred dollars per tree. Their perils include theft and vandalism, but not windstorm.

beats.text: Don't confuse that with tree removal: up to $1,000 per loss, $500 per tree, to remove trees felled by windstorm, hail, or weight of ice, snow or sleet. The tree must damage a covered structure or block a driveway or handicap ramp.
beats.say: Don't confuse that with tree removal: up to one thousand dollars per loss, five hundred dollars per tree, to remove trees felled by windstorm, hail, or weight of ice, snow or sleet. The tree must damage a covered structure or block a driveway or handicap ramp.

beats.text: Ordinance or law pays up to 10% of Coverage A, as additional insurance, for increased costs from enforcing building ordinances after a covered loss.
beats.say: Ordinance or law pays up to ten percent of Coverage A, as additional insurance, for increased costs from enforcing building ordinances after a covered loss.

scenes.q: Under the 2011 HO-3, a windstorm knocks down a healthy backyard tree. It hits nothing and blocks nothing. What do the tree additional coverages pay?
choices: Up to $500 to replace the tree
Up to $1,000 to remove the tree
scenes.why: Windstorm is not a covered peril for trees, shrubs and plants. Tree removal applies only if the tree damages a covered structure or blocks a driveway or handicap ramp.

beats.text: One more. A windstorm knocks down a healthy backyard tree. It hits nothing and blocks nothing. What do the tree coverages pay? Pick an answer.
beats.say: One more. A windstorm knocks down a healthy backyard tree. It hits nothing and blocks nothing. What do the tree coverages pay? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Nothing. Windstorm isn't a covered peril for trees. And tree removal needs damage to a covered structure, or a blocked driveway or ramp.
reveal.say: Nothing. Windstorm isn't a covered peril for trees. And tree removal needs damage to a covered structure, or a blocked driveway or ramp.

items: HO-2 named; HO-3 open on A and B; HO-5 open on A, B and C
HO-4: C and D only. HO-6 A: the unit's fixtures and improvements
Attached structures are A; detached are B, at 10% of A
HO-3: jewelry, firearms and silverware limits are theft only
HO-3 trees: 5% of A, not windstorm. Ordinance or law: 10% of A

beats.text: To recap. HO-2 is named perils, HO-3 is open on the buildings, and HO-5 is open on everything. HO-4 has C and D only.
beats.say: To recap. H O two is named perils, H O three is open on the buildings, and H O five is open on everything. H O four has C and D only.

beats.text: Attached structures are A; detached ones are B. HO-3 jewelry, firearms and silverware limits apply only to theft. And windstorm doesn't replace trees.
beats.say: Attached structures are A; detached ones are B. H O three jewelry, firearms and silverware limits apply only to theft. And windstorm doesn't replace trees.
